item.title: Skill: Voice-Matched Draft Editor

item.description: Say what you saw and when, not what the person is like. The phrases below describe a gap one area at a time.

item.title: Guide: How to write a performance review in 20 minutes
item.description: Collect the facts, choose a level for each area, build the review, write a three-line summary and check it. About 20 minutes.

item.title: Guide: How to write a cold email subject line
item.description: Say what the email is about, in the words the reader would use. Keep it short and true. No tricks, no fake "Re:", nothing the email does not deliver.

item.title: Guide: How to talk to an employee about a mistake: questions and opening lines
item.description: Talk in private, soon, and start with the facts. Ask what happened without blame, then ask what they need to put it right.

item.title: Guide: Follow-up email after no response: four you can copy
item.description: Send one short note 3 to 5 working days after the first email. Say why you wrote, give them an easy way out, and add one new useful thing each time.

item.title: Guide: Follow-up email after a meeting: four you can copy
item.description: Send it the same day. Say what you heard, what each of you will do and by when, and ask them to correct anything you got wrong.

item.title: Guide: First one on one with a new employee: what to ask
item.description: Plan about an hour in five parts: welcome, how they like to work, what is expected, how you will meet, agree and close. The questions below fit into it.

item.title: Guide: Cold email template for B2B: four you can copy
item.description: Say what you saw on their page, what you do, and ask one small question. Four sentences are enough. Only write what you can show is true.
